It is # spelled the way `unsafe_chr` below is: `unsafe_to_u8`. Crystal spells # it `to_u8!`, which is not a name in iyi (SPEC.md III.1.7) — those # declarations were accepted only because a macro expansion was # reparsed by the other language's rules, and no iyi source could call # one: `x.to_u8!` is `x.to_u8` with its error propagated. The callers # wanted the instruction: `memset`'s `value.to_u8!` is C's "converted to # unsigned char", and the checked form panics on 0x1ff where C writes 0xff. def to_i : Int32 def to_i32 : Int32 def to_i64 : Int64 def to_s(base : Int32) : String def to_s : String def to_u64 : UInt64 def to_u8 : UInt8 def unsafe_chr : Char def unsafe_div(other : Int32) : self def unsafe_div(other : Int64) : self def unsafe_div(other : UInt8) : self def unsafe_div(other : UInt64) : self def unsafe_mod(other : Int32) : self def unsafe_mod(other : Int64) : self def unsafe_mod(other : UInt8) : self def unsafe_mod(other : UInt64) : self def unsafe_shl(other : Int32) : self def unsafe_shl(other : Int64) : self def unsafe_shl(other : UInt8) : self def unsafe_shl(other : UInt64) : self def unsafe_shr(other : Int32) : self def unsafe_shr(other : Int64) : self def unsafe_shr(other : UInt8) : self def unsafe_shr(other : UInt64) : self def unsafe_to_f : Float64 def unsafe_to_f64 : Float64 def unsafe_to_i : Int32 def unsafe_to_i32 : Int32 def unsafe_to_i64 : Int64 def unsafe_to_u64 : UInt64 def unsafe_to_u8 : UInt8 def |(other : Int32) : self def |(other : Int64) : self def |(other : UInt8) : self def |(other : UInt64) : self def self.zero : self end # `import std/int` gives Int32 the rest of the integer tower's surface: # arithmetic and comparison with every integer type, `//`, `%`, `<<`, `>>`, # `<=>`, the bit counts and every `to_*` conversion (`iyi doc std/int`).
files.iyi doc Int64: # A 64-bit signed integer, the literal `1_i64`. struct Int64 < Int def !=(other : Int32) : Bool def !=(other : Int64) : Bool def !=(other : UInt8) : Bool def !=(other : UInt64) : Bool def !=(other : Float64) : Bool def !=(other : UInt16) : Bool def %(other : Int64) : Int64 def &(other : Int32) : self def &(other : Int64) : self def &(other : UInt8) : self def &(other : UInt64) : self def &*(other : Int32) : self def &*(other : Int64) : self def &*(other : UInt8) : self def &*(other : UInt64) : self def &+(other : Int32) : self def &+(other : Int64) : self def &+(other : UInt8) : self def &+(other : UInt64) : self def &-(other : Int32) : self def &-(other : Int64) : self def &-(other : UInt8) : self def &-(other : UInt64) : self def *(other : Int32) : self def *(other : Int64) : self def *(other : UInt8) : self def *(other : UInt64) : self def *(other : Float64) : Float64 def +(other : Int32) : self def +(other : Int64) : self def +(other : UInt8) : self def +(other : UInt64) : self def +(other : Float64) : Float64 def -(other : Int32) : self def -(other : Int64) : self def -(other : UInt8) : self def -(other : UInt64) : self def -(other : Float64) : Float64 def - Without it an `Int64` hashed to # its type, `Object#hash`'s default, so every key of a `Hash(Int64, V)` # or `Set(Int64)` went to one slot and each insert walked all the keys # before it: 80,000 inserts took 2.9 s and two million did not finish in # two minutes. `UInt64`, `UInt8`, `Char` and `Float64` were the same, # and `std/int`, which writes `hash` for the rest of the integer tower, # leaves the prelude's types to the prelude. def hash : Int32 def to_f : Float64 def to_f64 : Float64 # The checked form raises on overflow — which in this prelude is a panic, # since `__crystal_raise_overflow` prints and exits (SPEC.md III.1.4). # # The unchecked form is the conversion without the check, and a float # past the range saturates (NaN is 0), alike in every build. It is # spelled the way `unsafe_chr` below is: `unsafe_to_u8`. Crystal spells # it `to_u8!`, which is not a name in iyi (SPEC.md III.1.7) — those # declarations were accepted only because a macro expansion was # reparsed by the other language's rules, and no iyi source could call # one: `x.to_u8!` is `x.to_u8` with its error propagated. The callers # wanted the instruction: `memset`'s `value.to_u8!` is C's "converted to # unsigned char", and the checked form panics on 0x1ff where C writes 0xff. def to_i : Int32 def to_i32 : Int32 def to_i64 : Int64 # Writes digits backward using division on negative numbers so that # Int64::MIN (-9223372036854775808) does not overflow negation. The # digits are counted first and written straight into the string: they # went through an `Array(Int32)` of their own, an allocation and a # growth per number printed, and printing two million integers took # twice Go's time. def to_s(base : Int32) : String # Written by dividing the *negative* magnitude rather than negating it, # because `-Int64::MIN` is not an Int64: negation overflows and every # digit after it is wrong. `src/std/format.iyi` used to carry a second # definition of both of these with this shape, so what a program got # depended on whether the formatter had been loaded; there is one of each # now, here, where `Int32#to_s` already delegates. def to_s : String def to_u64 : UInt64 def to_u8 : UInt8 def unsafe_chr : Char def unsafe_div(other : Int32) : self def unsafe_div(other : Int64) : self def unsafe_div(other : UInt8) : self def unsafe_div(other : UInt64) : self def unsafe_mod(other : Int32) : self def unsafe_mod(other : Int64) : self def unsafe_mod(other : UInt8) : self def unsafe_mod(other : UInt64) : self def unsafe_shl(other : Int32) : self def unsafe_shl(other : Int64) : self def unsafe_shl(other : UInt8) : self def unsafe_shl(other : UInt64) : self def unsafe_shr(other : Int32) : self def unsafe_shr(other : Int64) : self def unsafe_shr(other : UInt8) : self def unsafe_shr(other : UInt64) : self def unsafe_to_f : Float64 def unsafe_to_f64 : Float64 def unsafe_to_i : Int32 def unsafe_to_i32 : Int32 def unsafe_to_i64 : Int64 def unsafe_to_u64 : UInt64 def unsafe_to_u8 : UInt8 def |(other : Int32) : self def |(other : Int64) : self def |(other : UInt8) : self def |(other : UInt64) : self def self.zero : self end # `import std/int` gives Int64 the rest of the integer tower's surface: # arithmetic and comparison with every integer type, `//`, `%`, `<<`, `>>`, # `<=>`, the bit counts and every `to_*` conversion (`iyi doc std/int`).
files.iyi doc Nil: # The absence of a value, and the only value of its type. struct Nil < Value def ==(other : Nil) : Bool def inspect : String def to_s : String end
files.iyi doc Object: # What the compiler emits instructions for — SPEC.md, "0.1.0", item 3. # # A `@[Primitive]` method has no body on purpose: the annotation names an # instruction the code generator writes at the call site. So this file is not # an implementation, it is the list of machine operations iyi admits, and its # shape is a language decision rather than a library one. # # **This is iyi's list, not Crystal's.** `src/primitives.cr` declares twelve # numeric types and crosses them with each other, which is 2,580 definitions # expanded on every build and **0.11 s of a 0.17 s front end** — measured by # deleting the block and building again. iyi crosses five, which is 445. # # The five are `Int32`, `Int64`, `UInt8`, `UInt64` and `Float64`: the default # integer, the one a byte count grows into, the byte itself, the one an address # and a size are, and a float. `UInt16` joins them for comparison alone, for # the reason written at the cross below: a wide character is compared on # every Windows path. `Int8`, `Int16`, `Int128` and the unsigned middle exist # as types and have no arithmetic, because no sample writes one — the same # rule the rest of the prelude is built on. Writing `1_i8 + 1_i8` is an # "undefined method" and that is the honest answer: 0.1.0 does not have # eight-bit arithmetic rather than having it slowly. # # **Comparison is not refused the same way, and that is a defect this file # cannot close.** `Object#==` answers `false` for anything no type claimed, # which is right about two objects and a lie about two numbers: without # `import std/int`, `1_i8 == 1_i8` is `false` rather than an error, and it # was `92_u16 == 92_u16` answering false that hid two Windows defects for a # week. Refusing it needs both sides' types at once, which a method body # does not have — a guard on the receiver alone refuses `5 == nil`, where # `false` is the correct answer, and it was measured doing exactly that to # eleven exercises. The fix belongs in overload resolution, where the # compiler knows both types; until then `UInt16` being in the cross is what # the library's own callers needed, and this paragraph is the rest of the truth. class Object def !=(other) : Bool def ==(other) : Bool # Case equality, what a `when` asks of each arm: equality, unless a type # answers with something stronger - a range, a class, a tuple. def ===(other) : Bool def class # Every type is usable as a `Hash` key, and one that has not said how it # hashes hashes to its type: correct and useless, every value of the type # in one slot, the honest default. A type used as a key defines `hash`. def hash : Int32 # `value.in?(a, b)` — the Kemal port's way of writing an alternation. On # `Object` because it is about the value, not about any one type of it. def in?(*values : *T) : Bool forall T # What a value looks like written down rather than printed: the two differ # for `nil` and strings, and `#{value.inspect}` shows a value is absent. def inspect : String # The type's own name, which is what a value that has said nothing about # itself can honestly print. A type that wants better defines its own. def to_s : String end
files.iyi doc Panicked: # What a *caught* panic answers as — III.1.4's "catchable at task # boundaries", made literal: reading a panicked task's value delivers # this instead of a re-raise, and III.1.3's machinery (`case`, `!`, # `.or`) handles it like any other failure. A panic nobody reads still # re-raises at the join: observed bugs are values, unobserved bugs are # loud. struct Panicked def message : String def new(text : String) def text : String end
files.iyi doc Pointer: # A raw address: `Pointer(T).malloc(n)` is `n` elements of untyped memory, # `[]` and `[]=` read and write them, nothing checks the bounds. struct Pointer(T) < Value def +(offset : Int64) : self def -(other : self) : Int64 def [](offset : Int32) : T def []=(offset : Int32, value : T) : T def address : UInt64 # Bytes, not elements: every caller here is copying string contents. def copy_from(source : Pointer(T), count : Int32) : Nil def new def realloc(size : UInt64) : self def value : T def value=(value : T) def self.malloc(size : UInt64) def self.new(address : UInt64) end
files.iyi doc Proc: function Proc(*T, R) < Value def call(*args : *T) : R end
files.iyi doc Program: # The running program: its arguments and its environment, on demand. class Program # The arguments after the program's own name, the way every shell # hands them over. def self.args : Array(String) # The directory the process is in, which is not what `PWD` says. # `PWD` is a variable a shell keeps: cmd and PowerShell never set it, # so on Windows every program that expanded a relative path panicked # ("no base given and PWD is not set"), and on POSIX it is a copy that # a program's own `Dir.cd` leaves behind. Nil when the platform has no # answer — wasm32-wasi resolves a path against a preopened directory # and names none — or when the directory is gone from under the # process. # # 4096 bytes covers POSIX's PATH_MAX and Windows' MAX_PATH; the second # try is for a Windows path built with `\\?\`, which reaches 32,767 # characters and up to three UTF-8 bytes each. def self.cwd : String | Nil # One variable, or nil. No map of everything: the asking program names # what it wants, and a tool that dumps its whole environment into a # structure was one `puts` away from leaking it. def self.env(name : String) : String | Nil end
files.iyi doc Range: # Ranges — SPEC.md, "0.1.0", item 3. # # The compiler expands a range literal to `Range.new(from, to, exclusive)` # (literal_expander.cr) and predefines the type to refer to it; with no # methods, `(1..10).each` was refused with "wrong number of arguments for # 'Range(B, E).new'", a constructor nobody wrote. A range here counts up by # one and stops: no `Enumerable`, no `step`, no reverse iteration. struct Range(B, E) # A range is a value, so two written the same way are the same range: # `Object#==` is identity, and `(1..3) == (1..3)` was false. `1..3` and # `1...3` differ, and that is the flag's whole job. def ==(other : self) : Bool # `when 1..5` is `(1..5) === x`: inclusion. `==` answered, and no arm matched. def ===(value) : Bool def begin : B # The inclusive walk stops *at* the end rather than stepping past it: with # `value <= @end` the last step left the type on the checked `+`, so # `(2147483645..2147483647).each` panicked with "arithmetic overflow" at # the value it was asked to yield last. def each(& : (B -> Nil)) : Nil def end : E # `1...10` excludes its end, `1..10` includes it. def exclusive? : Bool # And hashing follows equality, or equal ranges would land in two slots. def hash : Int32 # The three a range is written for: a value per position, the positions # that answer, and the total. def map(& : (B -> U)) : Array(U) forall U def new(begin __arg0 : B, end __arg1 : E, exclusive : Bool) def select(& : (B -> Bool)) : Array(B) def size : Int32 def sum : B def to_a : Array(B) # `1..5` and `1...3`, each end inspected and a nil one left out, as the # other library writes one; `Object#to_s` printed `Range(Int32, Int32)`. def to_s : String end
files.iyi doc Reference: # What every class instance is: a pointer to its fields, compared and # hashed by identity unless the class says otherwise. # # That was this comment's promise and nothing kept it: `Object#==` answers # false, so an instance was not even equal to itself, and a `Set(Node)` # never found the node just added to it nor a `Hash(Node, V)` its key. # Identity is `==` now, and the hash is the address. A class that writes # its own `==` says what equal means, and the address would part two # instances it calls equal - so one that writes `==` and no `hash` keeps # the type's id, correct for any `==` and one slot for every instance, the # default `Object#hash` explains. class Reference def ==(other : Reference) : Bool def hash : Int32 def new def object_id : UInt64 end
files.iyi doc Set: # The one set — "have I seen this", with nothing attached to the answer. # # A `Hash` whose values are nothing: the same dense keys in insertion # order and the same index over them, so `add`, `includes?` and `delete` # cost what the hash's do and iteration reads back in the order things # went in. It is a wrapper rather than a copy of `hash.iyi` because the # index is the part worth getting right once. The sample that asked for # it (`samples/iyi/visited.iyi`) walks a graph with a cycle in it, and # `add` answering whether the element was new is the one bit that walk # needs. class Set(T) # Not in `other`, in this order; `other` may be of another element type. def -(other : Set(U)) : Set(T) forall U # True when the element was not there before. def add(value : T) : Bool # True when the element was there. def delete(value : T) : Bool # Every element, in the order it went in. def each(& : (T -> Nil)) : Nil def empty? : Bool def includes?(value : T) : Bool def inspect : String def new def size : Int32 def to_a : Array(T) # `Set{"a", "b"}`, in insertion order, elements inspected. def to_s : String end
files.iyi doc String: # Text — SPEC.md, "0.1.0", item 3. # # The compiler declares `String`'s fields itself — `@bytesize`, `@length` and # `@c`, in that order, in `Program#initialize` — because codegen lays out # string literals before any prelude is read. So this file reopens a type that # already has its shape and only says what can be done with it. class String # `"ab" * -3` answered `""` where the other library raises (III.1.7a). # The size is a division, so the refusal names the string: `"abcd" * # 600_000_000` panicked "arithmetic overflow", the machine's adder. def *(count : Int32) : String def +(other : String) : String # Byte order, which for ASCII is dictionary order with the capitals first; # a prefix sorts before what it prefixes. What `sorted` and `sorted_by` # ask of a string. def <(other : String) : Bool # Thirty-two bytes a step while they last, then one at a time, and the # same string is itself: a byte a step was eleven times Python's `==`, # 230 ms for 1,000 compares of equal megabytes. No load needs alignment. def ==(other : String) : Bool # A negative *start* counts from the end, the same wrap as the one-index # form. *count* stays non-negative: a negative count is not a wrap, it is a # mistake, and it raises for that reason rather than being silently clamped. def [](start : Int32, count : Int32) : String # The character at *index*, asked for by `samples/iyi/calc`, which scans # its input a character at a time. Byte-indexed: a byte is the character # for ASCII, and `each_char` is the decoded walk. A negative index counts # from the end; out of range after that wrap raises, `[]?` answers nil. def [](index : Int32) : Char def []?(index : Int32) : Char | ::Nil # Where *search* first starts at or after byte *offset* - counted from # the end when negative - in bytes, as Crystal's `byte_index` answers. # Naive while that is cheap, and Rabin-Karp - one rolling hash per # position, bytes compared only where it matches - once more than four # bytes a position have been compared: a needle that keeps almost # matching, `"a" * 1000 + "b"` in a run of `a`, made the naive loop # n * m, 222 ms for a megabyte. def byte_index(search : String, offset : Int32 = 0) : Int32 | ::Nil def bytesize : Int32 # `'\n'` is a line's end, so it takes the `\r` before it, or a lone `\r` # in its place, as the other library's does: `"a\r\n".chomp('\n')` is "a". def chomp(char : Char) : String # The other half of `upcase`, ASCII for the same reason. def downcase : String # Every character in order, decoded, as many as `size` counts: it yielded # one per byte, so `"héllo".size` was 5 and `each_char` ran six times. # Indexing stays byte-indexed (`[]` above), as `samples/iyi/calc` scans. # A byte that begins no character is one U+FFFD, as in the other library: # a lead byte took the bytes after it whatever they were, C3 41 was the # one character U+00C1, and `"a" C3 '"'` swallowed the quote. def each_char(& : (Char -> Nil)) : Nil def empty? : Bool def ends_with?(suffix : String) : Bool # FNV-1a over the bytes: three lines, no table, and good enough for a # linear-probing table of a few dozen entries. def hash : Int32 def includes?(other : String) : Bool # Where a character first is, or nil: the question a parser asks before # it cuts. def index(char : Char) : Int32 | ::Nil # The literal that spells it, escaped as the other library's, a byte that # is no UTF-8 as `\x`: unescaped, `["a\", \"b"]` printed as two strings. def inspect : String def lchop(char : Char) : String # The lines of a text, blank ones included, a final newline ending the last # line; `\r\n` ends one too, and a last `\r` with no `\n` after it is kept: # `"1\r\n".lines[0].to_i` panicked where `File.read_lines` read 1. def lines : Array(String) def ljust(width : Int32, pad : Char = ' ') : String # Pad on the left (rjust) or the right (ljust) to *width*, in characters # as `size` counts them, the pad as its own bytes: in bytes, # `"héllo".rjust(7, '.')` answered a string of `size` 6, and a `'·'` # written as one byte left a lone continuation byte in the result. def rjust(width : Int32, pad : Char = ' ') : String # A zero `@length` on a non-empty string is "not counted yet", which is # how the other library's own code leaves a string it builds: `to_json`'s # result answered `size` 0 here while the field was returned as it stood. # The layout is shared on purpose (SPEC.md Part V item 12), so the # invariant is too. The count is of what `each_char` yields, a byte that # begins no character one U+FFFD. def size : Int32 # The pieces between separators, empty ones included: `"a,,b".split(',')` # is three, `"a,".split(',')` is two, and `"".split(',')` is one empty # piece - the count the other library gives, so a program reads the same # under both. def split(separator : Char) : Array(String) # The three the Kemal port's path joining needs, byte-indexed: the same # as by character while the strings are ASCII. def starts_with?(prefix : String) : Bool # A `Char` above ASCII is more than one byte, and these narrowed it to one # through a *checked* convert, so `"a☃b".index('☃')` died of "arithmetic # overflow". Each compares the character's own bytes now. def starts_with?(char : Char) : Bool # Without `Char#whitespace?`'s characters at either end, decoded: it read # bytes, and `"b\u00A0".strip` kept the space the other library takes. def strip : String # The double nearest the decimal written here, correctly rounded: the # digits and the exponent are read into the printer's bignum and the # quotient taken to 54 bits with a sticky remainder, so what `to_s` # wrote reads back as the same double, every time, and "0.1" is the # double the literal `0.1` is. Accepts `-1.5`, `2.5e-3`, `1E10`, `.5`, # `7.`, `Infinity`, `NaN`, with `Char#whitespace?` around as `to_i?` # takes it; raises "not a number" for anything else. def to_f : Float64 # The number this string spells - an optional sign and decimal digits, # the whole string - as `samples/iyi/calc` reads a token. Raises on # anything else, as the other library's does (SPEC.md III.1.7a): a # silent 0 for `"oops"` is wrong twice; `to_i?` answers nil for it. def to_i : Int32 # Around the digits, `Char#whitespace?` is skipped as the other # library's `whitespace: true` skips it (`"42\n".to_i?` was nil). Read # as a *negative* magnitude, which holds every value the type has: # `2147483648` accumulated and negated, `Int32::MIN` overflowed on its # last digit, a panic rather than the `nil` a `?` promises. def to_i? : Int32 | ::Nil def to_s : String def to_unsafe : Pointer(UInt8) # ASCII only, and the samples are ASCII. A prelude that folded case for # every alphabet would be a Unicode table, which is more lines than this # whole file and not what any sample is about. def upcase : String def self.build(capacity : Int32 = 64, & : (String::Builder -> _)) : String # Interpolation is a call the compiler writes: `"a#{b}"` reaches here as # `String.interpolation("a", b)` (`LiteralExpander#expand`). The overloads # are what let the common shapes avoid work — a single string is itself. def self.interpolation(value : String) : String def self.interpolation(value) : String def self.interpolation(*values : *T) : String forall T # Allocates *bytesize* bytes, hands the buffer to the block to fill, and # returns the string that results. The character count is left at zero, # "not counted yet", for `size` to scan the first time it is asked: most # strings built here - an encoding, a join, a line - are never asked, and # counting them all was a second pass over every byte built. # # The byte after the last is a NUL, as a literal's is, so `to_unsafe` is # a C string: `std/process` and `std/debug` hand one to the platform as a # path. The byte was allocated for that and never written, and a string's # chunk is atomic - not cleared - so a chunk that had held a longer # string kept that string's byte there. Measured on Windows after a # collection that freed longer strings: 961 of 1,000 strings built after # it had no terminator, and `Process.run` of a path built that way # answered "no such program" for a file that was there. def self.new(bytesize : Int32, & : (Pointer(UInt8) -> Nil)) : String end
files.iyi doc Struct: # A struct is its fields, as the other library's `Struct#==` has it: two are # equal when each field is. `Object#==` answers false, so a struct was not # equal to itself - `b == b` was false and `{b => 1}[b]?` nil. `Object#hash` # stays correct for it, one slot a type; a struct that is a key writes one. struct Struct < Value def ==(other : self) : Bool end
files.iyi doc Symbol: # A name that compares by identity: `:ok`, `:err`. struct Symbol < Value def !=(other : Symbol) : Bool def ==(other : Symbol) : Bool def hash : Int32 def to_i : Int32 def to_s : String end
files.iyi doc Tuple: # A tuple written the way it is written: `{1, "a"}`. The compiler lays a # tuple out and answers `[]`; what it looks like printed is the prelude's, # one element per position, each inspected. tuple Tuple(*T) < Value # Two tuples are the same value when their members are. `Object#==` is # false, so `{1, 2} == {1, 2}` was, and a tuple key was never found in a # `Hash`. The count is read # once: walking `other.size` while pushing grew it along with this deque # when the two were one, so `d.concat(d)` never ended. def concat(other : Deque(T)) : Deque(T) def concat(items : Array(T)) : Deque(T) # Removes and answers the element at index; the shorter side closes # the gap. def delete_at(index : Int32) : T # A copy with the same elements, contiguous from slot 0. def dup : Deque(T) # size copies of value. def initialize(size : Int32, value : T) # An empty deque with room for initial_capacity elements before it grows. def initialize(initial_capacity : Int32) # An empty deque; the first push allocates. def initialize # Inserts value before index; `size` appends, `-1` appends too (the # position after the last). The shorter side moves. def insert(index : Int32, value : T) : Deque(T) def inspect : String # The array's elements, in its order. def self.new(items : Array(T)) : Deque(T) # size elements, each what the block answers for its index. def self.new(size : Int32, & : (Int32 -> T)) : Deque(T) # Removes the last n elements, or all of them when there are fewer. def pop(n : Int32) : Nil # Removes and answers the last element. def pop : T def pop? : T | ::Nil # Appends value; answers the deque. def push(value : T) : Deque(T) # Rotates in place so that the element at position n comes first; a # negative n rotates the other way. A full buffer only moves `@start`; # otherwise the shorter end is walked around. def rotate_in_place(n : Int32 = 1) : Deque(T) # A copy rotated by n, this deque untouched. def rotated(n : Int32 = 1) : Deque(T) # Removes the first n elements, or all of them when there are fewer. def shift(n : Int32) : Nil # Removes and answers the first element. def shift : T def shift? : T | ::Nil def size : Int32 # `Deque{1, 2, 3}`, elements inspected. def to_s : String # The element at a logical index, no bounds check; `Indexable#[]` does # the checking. def unsafe_fetch(index : Int32) : T # Prepends value; answers the deque. def unshift(value : T) : Deque(T) end impl Std::Indexable::Indexable for Deque(T) forall T end impl Std::Indexable::IndexableMutable for Deque(T) forall T def unsafe_put(index : Int32, value : T) : T end impl Std::Enumerable::Enumerable for Deque(T) forall T end

files.iyi doc std/eiy: module std/eiy pub struct Eiy # Collects what a template prints, for `render` or for a caller that wants # the text rather than a stream. class Buffer def initialize def print(text : String) : Nil def print(value) : Nil # `print`, the one verb a template's target has, so a Buffer can be one. def to_s(io) : Nil def to_s : String end class Lexer class Token enum Type : Int32 String = 0 Output = 1 Control = 2 EOF = 3 end def column_number : Int32 def column_number=(value : Int32) : Int32 def control? : Bool def eof? : Bool def initialize def line_number : Int32 def line_number=(value : Int32) : Int32 def output? : Bool def string? : Bool def suppress_leading : Bool def suppress_leading=(value : Bool) : Bool def suppress_leading? : Bool def suppress_trailing : Bool def suppress_trailing=(value : Bool) : Bool def suppress_trailing? : Bool def type : Type def type=(value : Type) : Type def value : String def value=(value : String) : String end # Why the last `next_token?` answered nil, or nil while it has not. def error : String | ::Nil def initialize(string : String) # The next token; the same `Token` object is reused, so copy what is # needed before asking again. files.iyi doc std/file: module std/file pub alias File = ::File # Linux: the kernel's own calls, as `socket` and the prelude make them # (SPEC.md III.9: an own-prelude object asks libc for nothing). The # shape is libc's, so the callers above read the same; a failure comes # back as the negative errno the kernel answers, which every caller # here reads as "not zero". `realpath` is a walk over `readlinkat` and # `newfstatat`, since libc's is a library function and not a call. pub struct LibC # x86_64 `struct stat`, 144 bytes, the layout glibc shares with the kernel. struct Stat def initialize def st_atime : Timespec def st_blksize : Int64 def st_blocks : Int64 def st_ctime : Timespec def st_dev : UInt64 def st_gid : Int32 def st_ino : UInt64 def st_mode : Int32 def st_mtime : Timespec def st_nlink : UInt64 def st_pad0 : Int32 def st_rdev : UInt64 def st_reserved0 : Int64 def st_reserved1 : Int64 def st_reserved2 : Int64 def st_size : Int64 def st_uid : Int32 end struct Timespec def initialize def tv_nsec : Int64 def tv_sec : Int64 end def self.access(path : ::Pointer(UInt8), mode : Int32) : Int32 def self.chmod(path : ::Pointer(UInt8), mode : Int32) : Int32 def self.chown(path : ::Pointer(UInt8), owner : Int32, group : Int32) : Int32 def self.fstat(fd : Int32, buf : ::Pointer(Stat)) : Int32 def self.ftruncate(fd : Int32, length : Int64) : Int32 def initialize def self.link(oldpath : ::Pointer(UInt8), newpath : ::Pointer(UInt8)) : Int32 def self.lstat(path : ::Pointer(UInt8), buf : ::Pointer(Stat)) : Int32 def self.readlink(path : ::Pointer(UInt8), buf : ::Pointer(UInt8), bufsiz : UInt64) : Int64 # The absolute path with every `.`, `..` and symbolic link resolved, or # null when a component does not exist. Forty links deep is the limit, # as it is in libc. def self.realpath(path : ::Pointer(UInt8), resolved : ::Pointer(UInt8)) : ::Pointer(UInt8) def self.rename(oldpath : ::Pointer(UInt8), newpath : ::Pointer(UInt8)) : Int32 def self.stat(path : ::Pointer(UInt8), buf : ::Pointer(Stat)) : Int32 def self.symlink(target : ::Pointer(UInt8), linkpath : ::Pointer(UInt8)) : Int32 def self.sys(number : Int64, a : Int64, b : Int64, c : Int64, d : Int64 = 0_i64, e : Int64 = 0_i64) : Int64 def self.truncate(path : ::Pointer(UInt8), length : Int64) : Int32 # *sec* 0 is "now" (a null timespec, as utimensat documents). Otherwise # atime and mtime are both that Unix second. def self.utimensat(path : ::Pointer(UInt8), sec : Int64) : Int32 end class ::File def self.basename(path : String | Path, suffix : String | ::Nil = nil) : String def self.chmod(path : String | Path, mode : Int32) : Nil def self.chown(path : String | Path, uid : Int32, gid : Int32) : Nil def self.directory?(path : String | Path) : Bool def self.dirname(path : String | Path) : String # A line at a time, off the file as it is read: it read the whole file # into an array of its lines first, so a log of any size was the # program's memory twice over before the first line was seen. A 1xx, 204 or 304 # has no content (RFC 9110 §15), and writes neither a body nor a length # of its own (§8.6): the body was read by the client as the start of the # next answer, and `Content-Length: 0` on a 304 told a cache that the # resource had become empty. def self.format_response(response : Response, head : Bool, close : Bool) : String # One connection: requests until the client is done. Writes land at the cursor and grow the # buffer; reads advance the cursor; `to_s` is the whole buffer. pub class Memory < ::IyiIO # Forgets every byte; the cursor returns to the start. def clear : Nil def close : Nil def closed? : Bool def empty? : Bool def eof? : Bool def flush : Nil def initialize(capacity : Int32 = 64) # A buffer holding a copy of `text`'s bytes, the cursor at its start. def initialize(text : String) # The cursor, in bytes from the start. Int64, as a file's position is: # with `std/file` imported every `IyiIO` has a `pos : Int64`, and a # narrower answer here made `pos` on any `IyiIO` fail to compile. def pos : Int64 def pos=(position : Int32) : Nil # The cursor moved through an `IyiIO`: the stream's own position, not # the descriptor's that `std/file` would move. def pos=(position : Int64) : Int64 def read_all : String def read_byte : UInt8 | ::Nil def read_bytes(count : Int32) : String def read_line(chomp : Bool = false) : String | ::Nil def rewind : Nil # Bytes held, written or given. def size : Int32 def to_s : String def write(bytes : Pointer(UInt8), count : Int32) : Nil end # One stream written to several. `close` closes this writer, not the # streams behind it. pub class MultiWriter < ::IyiIO def close : Nil def closed? : Bool def eof? : Bool def flush : Nil def initialize(writers : Array(IyiIO)) def read_all : String def read_byte : UInt8 | ::Nil def read_bytes(count : Int32) : String def read_line(chomp : Bool = false) : String | ::Nil def write(bytes : Pointer(UInt8), count : Int32) : Nil end # At most `limit` bytes of another stream. pub class Sized < Reader def eof? : Bool def initialize(io : IyiIO, limit : Int32) def read_all : String def read_byte : UInt8 | ::Nil # The inner stream is asked for at most 64 KB at a time: a descriptor # stream's `read_bytes` allocates the whole count before it reads, and # `read_all` under a limit of Int32::MAX took 2 GB to read two bytes. def read_bytes(count : Int32) : String # Bytes the limit still allows, whether or not the stream has them. def remaining : Int32 def write(bytes : Pointer(UInt8), count : Int32) : Nil end class ::IyiIO def <<(value) : self # Everything left in `source` (at most `limit` bytes) written to # `target`, which is flushed; answers the number of bytes moved. def self.copy(source : IyiIO, target : IyiIO, limit : Int32 | ::Nil = nil) : Int64 def each_line(chomp : Bool = false, &block : (String -> Nil)) : Nil # Every remaining line, `chomp` dropping the line ends. def lines(chomp : Bool = false) : Array(String) # The next byte, or nil at the end. def read_byte : UInt8 | ::Nil # The next UTF-8 code point, or nil at the end. A lead byte that is not # one (a continuation byte, C0/C1, F5 and above), a continuation byte that # is not one, or a sequence the stream ends inside is refused. The first # continuation byte is held to the range its lead allows (Unicode Table # 3-7), so an overlong form, a surrogate and a code point past U+10FFFF # are refused at the byte that gives them away, not decoded into a Char # outside Unicode. def read_char : Char | ::Nil def write_byte(byte : UInt8) : Nil end
files.iyi doc std/iterator: module std/iterator # The sources are classes, as the other library's are: an adaptor keeps # its source by value, and a struct source was copied into it, so # `it.first(2).to_a` and then `it.to_a` gave [1, 2] and [1, 2, 3, 4] where # the other library gives [1, 2] and [3, 4]. Shared, the adaptor's pulls # are the source's. An adaptor that keeps a count, a flag or a buffer is # the source of whatever is built on it, so it is a class for the same # reason: as a struct it was copied too, and `t = it.take(3)`, # `t.first(2).to_a` and then `t.to_a` gave [3, 4, 5] where the other # library gives [3], `each_cons` handed its first window out again and # `step` and `with_index` restarted their strides and counts. An adaptor # that keeps only its sources, a block or a size stays a struct: a copy of # it pulls from the same place. # # Each type defines `next` once and its `impl` names only `Elem`, as # `NumericStepIterator` (std/steppable) does: every adaptor carried the same # `next` twice, once on the type and once in the `impl`. pub class ArrayIterator(T) def initialize(array : Array(T)) def next : T | Stop end pub class ChainIterator(I1, I2, T) def initialize(iter1 : I1, iter2 : I2) def next : T | Stop end pub struct CompactMapIterator(I, T, U) def initialize(iter : I, func : (T -> U | ::Nil)) def next : U | Stop end pub class ConsIterator(I, T) def initialize(iter : I, n : Int32) def next : Array(T) | Stop end pub class CycleIterator(I, T) def initialize(iter : I) def next : T | Stop end pub class CycleNIterator(I, T) def initialize(iter : I, n : Int32) def next : T | Stop end # The source an endless range gets: it counts up by one from the beginning # with no end, as an endless range does in the other library. pub class EndlessRangeIterator(B) def initialize(current : B) def next : B end pub class EntryIterator(K, V) def initialize(hash : Hash(K, V)) def next : Tuple(K, V) | Stop end pub class FlatMapIterator(I, T, U) def initialize(iter : I, func : (T -> Array(U))) def next : U | Stop end pub trait Iterator type Elem def all?(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Bool # Whether an element is truthy, which is what the other library's `any?` # answers: this said whether there was an element at all, so # `Iterator.of([false, false]).any?` was true. It pulls until it meets a # truthy element, and what it pulled is gone: an iterator is a pull, so a # predicate over one cannot be free. For a source with no `false` in it # that is one element. The block form below reads as much as it has to # and no more. Said here because a method spelled like a question that # quietly takes elements is the kind of thing a caller finds out from the # answer to the *next* question. def any? : Bool def any?(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Bool def chain(other : O) : ChainIterator(self, O, Elem | O::Elem) forall O : Iterator def compact_map(&func : (Elem -> U | ::Nil)) : CompactMapIterator(self, Elem, U) forall U def count : Int32 def count(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Int32 def cycle(n : Int32) : CycleNIterator(self, Elem) def cycle : CycleIterator(self, Elem) def each(& : (Elem -> Nil)) : Nil def each_cons(n : Int32) : ConsIterator(self, Elem) def each_slice(n : Int32) : SliceIterator(self, Elem) # Nil when nothing matched, which is what `Enumerable#find` and `Array#find` # answer: not finding is the ordinary outcome of a search, and a caller who # wants the panic writes `|| raise` as the prelude does. `first?`/`first` # below keeps its pair — an exhausted iterator has no first element, which # is a question with no answer. def find(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Elem | ::Nil def first(n : Int32) : TakeIterator(self, Elem) def first : Elem def first? : Elem | ::Nil def flat_map(&func : (Elem -> Array(U))) : FlatMapIterator(self, Elem, U) forall U def map(&func : (Elem -> U)) : MapIterator(self, Elem, U) forall U def max : Elem where Elem : Comparable # The largest, or nil when there is none. `max?`/`max` is a real pair: # an empty source has no largest element, so the plain name raising is # the common case. This file keeps the same pair for `first?`/`first`, # and answers `find` with nil, where not finding is the ordinary outcome. def max? : Elem | ::Nil where Elem : Comparable def min : Elem where Elem : Comparable # And the same pair at the other end. def min? : Elem | ::Nil where Elem : Comparable abstract def next : Elem | Stop def none?(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Bool # Convenience constructor for arrays. def self.of(array : Array(T)) : ArrayIterator(T) forall T # An endless range counts up for as long as it is pulled, as the other # library's does: `Iterator.of((1..)).first(3).to_a` was accepted here # and then refused from inside `RangeIterator#next`, "expected argument # #1 to 'Int32#<' to be ... not Nil", a line of this file. A beginless # range has no first element to count from, and is refused at the call. def self.of(range : Range(B, Nil)) : EndlessRangeIterator(B) forall B def self.of(range : Range(Nil, E)) : Nil forall E def self.of(range : Range(B, E)) : RangeIterator(B, E) forall B, E def self.of_entries(hash : Hash(K, V)) : EntryIterator(K, V) forall K, V def self.of_keys(hash : Hash(K, V)) : KeyIterator(K, V) forall K, V def self.of_values(hash : Hash(K, V)) : ValueIterator(K, V) forall K, V def product : Elem where Elem : Num def reduce(initial : U, & : (U, Elem -> U)) : U forall U def reduce?(& : (Elem, Elem -> Elem)) : Elem | ::Nil def reject(&func : (Elem -> Bool)) : RejectIterator(self, Elem) def select(&func : (Elem -> Bool)) : SelectIterator(self, Elem) def size : Int32 def skip(n : Int32) : SkipIterator(self, Elem) def skip_while(&func : (Elem -> Bool)) : SkipWhileIterator(self, Elem) def step(n : Int32) : StepIterator(self, Elem) def sum : Elem where Elem : Num def take(n : Int32) : TakeIterator(self, Elem) def take_while(&func : (Elem -> Bool)) : TakeWhileIterator(self, Elem) def to_a : Array(Elem) def with_index(offset : Int32 = 0) : WithIndexIterator(self, Elem) def with_index(offset : Int32 = 0, & : (Elem, Int32 -> Nil)) : Nil # Bounded, as `Enumerable#zip` is (SPEC.md II.6 finding 6). Unbounded, a # zip with an array was refused from inside this file, "undefined # constant O::Elem" at the line below, and a chain with one from # `ChainIterator#next`; with `forall O : Iterator` the refusal names the # caller's line, the argument's type and `O`. A chain of two element # types yields either, as the other library's does: it was a return-type # error inside `ChainIterator`. def zip(other : O) : ZipIterator(self, Elem, O, O::Elem) forall O : Iterator end # The three views of a hash, in insertion order. Each takes its snapshot of # the hash once, when built — `Hash#keys` and `Hash#values` allocate a fresh # array per call, so asking per element was a copy of the table per step — # and then walks that snapshot, so a hash that changes under the iterator # does not change what it yields. pub class KeyIterator(K, V) def initialize(hash : Hash(K, V)) def next : K | Stop end pub struct MapIterator(I, T, U) def initialize(iter : I, func : (T -> U)) def next : U | Stop end # Counts up by one from the range's beginning, the way the prelude's # `Range#each` does, and stops at the end rather than stepping past it: # on an inclusive range whose end is the type's largest value, the step # after the last element would overflow. pub class RangeIterator(B, E) def initialize(range : Range(B, E)) def next : B | Stop end pub struct RejectIterator(I, T) def initialize(iter : I, func : (T -> Bool)) def next : T | Stop end pub struct SelectIterator(I, T) def initialize(iter : I, func : (T -> Bool)) def next : T | Stop end pub class SkipIterator(I, T) def initialize(iter : I, n : Int32) def next : T | Stop end pub class SkipWhileIterator(I, T) def initialize(iter : I, func : (T -> Bool)) def next : T | Stop end pub struct SliceIterator(I, T) def initialize(iter : I, n : Int32) def next : Array(T) | Stop end pub class StepIterator(I, T) def initialize(iter : I, by : Int32) def next : T | Stop end pub struct Stop def initialize end pub class TakeIterator(I, T) def initialize(iter : I, n : Int32) def next : T | Stop end pub class TakeWhileIterator(I, T) def initialize(iter : I, func : (T -> Bool)) def next : T | Stop end pub class ValueIterator(K, V) def initialize(hash : Hash(K, V)) def next : V | Stop end pub class WithIndexIterator(I, T) def initialize(iter : I, offset : Int32) def next : Tuple(T, Int32) | Stop end pub struct ZipIterator(I1, T1, I2, T2) def initialize(iter1 : I1, iter2 : I2) # Asks the second source only when the first has an element. Asking both # took one from the second each time the first had run out: after # `a.zip(b).to_a` with `a` = [1] and `b` = [10, 20, 30], `b.next` # answered 30 where the other library and Python's `zip` answer 20. def next : Tuple(T1, T2) | Stop end impl Iterator for EndlessRangeIterator(B) forall B end impl Iterator for ArrayIterator(T) forall T end impl Iterator for RangeIterator(B, E) forall B, E end impl Iterator for KeyIterator(K, V) forall K, V end impl Iterator for ValueIterator(K, V) forall K, V end impl Iterator for EntryIterator(K, V) forall K, V end impl Iterator for MapIterator(I, T, U) forall I, T, U end impl Iterator for SelectIterator(I, T) forall I, T end impl Iterator for RejectIterator(I, T) forall I, T end impl Iterator for TakeIterator(I, T) forall I, T end impl Iterator for TakeWhileIterator(I, T) forall I, T end impl Iterator for SkipIterator(I, T) forall I, T end impl Iterator for SkipWhileIterator(I, T) forall I, T end impl Iterator for ZipIterator(I1, T1, I2, T2) forall I1, T1, I2, T2 end impl Iterator for ChainIterator(I1, I2, T) forall I1, I2, T end impl Iterator for FlatMapIterator(I, T, U) forall I, T, U end impl Iterator for SliceIterator(I, T) forall I, T end impl Iterator for ConsIterator(I, T) forall I, T end impl Iterator for WithIndexIterator(I, T) forall I, T end impl Iterator for CycleIterator(I, T) forall I, T end impl Iterator for CycleNIterator(I, T) forall I, T end impl Iterator for StepIterator(I, T) forall I, T end impl Iterator for CompactMapIterator(I, T, U) forall I, T, U end
files.iyi doc std/json: module std/json # `derive serializable`, in a struct or class whose fields are written with # their types: the type reads and writes itself as a JSON object, a key per # field, named as the field is. # # pub struct Coord # getter x : Float64 # getter name : String # derive serializable # end # # Coord.from_json(%({"x": 1.5, "name": "a"})).x # => 1.5 # coord.to_json # => {"x":1.5,"name":"a"} # # A field's value is read and written as `JSON.read_value` and # `JSON.write_value` read and write its type: the built-in values, an # `Array` or `Hash(String, V)` of them, an `Any`, another serializable # type. A key the type has no field for is passed over; a field with no # key keeps its default when it is written with one, as does a field with # a default whose key holds `null` where its type does not admit nil; a # field with neither is refused by name unless its type admits `nil`, # which it then holds. It is what the other library's `include # JSON::Serializable` writes, and the derive runs once, in the type's own # module (SPEC.md II.4), so a consumer calls the methods without the macro. pub macro serializable(declaration) # One JSON value of any kind, the result of `JSON.parse`. The `as_x` methods # panic when the value is of another kind; the `as_x?` ones answer `nil`. pub struct Any alias Type = Nil | Bool | Int64 | Float64 | String | Array(Any) | Hash(String, Any) # Equal when the values are: an integer equals the float with the same # value, arrays element by element, objects key by key in any order. def ==(other : Any) : Bool def [](index : Int32) : Any def [](key : String) : Any def []?(index : Int32) : Any | ::Nil def []?(key : String) : Any | ::Nil def as_a : Array(Any) def as_a? : Array(Any) | ::Nil def as_bool : Bool def as_bool? : Bool | ::Nil # A float, or an integer read as one. def as_f : Float64 def as_f? : Float64 | ::Nil def as_h : Hash(String, Any) def as_h? : Hash(String, Any) | ::Nil def as_i : Int32 def as_i64 : Int64 def as_i64? : Int64 | ::Nil def as_i? : Int32 | ::Nil def as_nil : Nil def as_s : String def as_s? : String | ::Nil def dig(key : String) : Any def dig(index : Int32) : Any def dig(k : String, *subkeys : String | Int32) : Any def dig(idx : Int32, *subkeys : String | Int32) : Any def dig?(key : String) : Any | ::Nil def dig?(index : Int32) : Any | ::Nil def dig?(k : String, *subkeys : String | Int32) : Any | ::Nil def dig?(idx : Int32, *subkeys : String | Int32) : Any | ::Nil protected def float_value? : Float64 | ::Nil # Consistent with `==`: a whole float hashes as the integer it equals, an # object's hash does not depend on the order its keys were written in. def hash : Int32 def initialize(raw : Type) def inspect : String # The kind of value this is, in the word a refusal uses: `null`, `bool`, # `integer`, `float`, `string`, `array` or `object`. def kind : String def self.new(val : Int32) : Any def raw : Type # How many elements an array or an object holds. A scalar has no size. def size : Int32 def size? : Int32 | ::Nil def to_ascii_json : String def to_json : String def to_pretty_json(indent : String = " ") : String # A string as itself and null as nothing, as `YAML::Any#to_s` and the # other library answer them; a number, a boolean or a collection as its # JSON text. A string was its JSON text too, so `"hello #{doc["name"]}"` # printed `hello "Ada"`, and null printed `null`. def to_s : String end # Writes a document one value at a time. `indent=` makes it pretty; # `ascii_only=` escapes every non-ASCII code point. pub class Builder def array(& : (-> Nil)) : Nil def ascii_only : Bool def ascii_only=(value : Bool) : Bool def bool(val : Bool) : Nil # Whether no value has been written yet. def empty? : Bool def end_array : Nil def end_object : Nil def field(name : String, val : Any) : Nil def field(name : String, val : String) : Nil def field(name : String, val : Int32) : Nil def field(name : String, val : Int64) : Nil def field(name : String, val : Float64) : Nil def field(name : String, val : Bool) : Nil def field(name : String, val : Nil) : Nil # A key; the value that follows it is written by the next call. A key # whose text is one this object already holds is refused, naming both: # the reader refuses a duplicate key, and the builder wrote one - a key # given twice, or two Strings whose bytes are not UTF-8 and are both # written as U+FFFD (`{"a\xFF" => 1, "a\xFE" => 2}` was written # `{"a\uFFFD":1,"a\uFFFD":2}`, and `JSON.parse` refused it). def field(name : String) : Nil def field(name : String, & : (-> Nil)) : Nil def indent=(spaces : Int32) : Nil def indent=(str : String) : Nil def initialize def max_nesting : Int32 def max_nesting=(value : Int32) : Int32 def null : Nil def number(val : Int32) : Nil def number(val : Int64) : Nil def number(val : UInt8) : Nil def number(val : UInt64) : Nil def number(val : Float64) : Nil def object(& : (-> Nil)) : Nil # Text written as it is: the caller's own JSON. def raw(str : String) : Nil def start_array : Nil def start_object : Nil def string(val : String) : Nil # The document's text. A container still open or no value written at all # is not a document, and is refused. def to_s : String end pub struct JSON # Text written through a `Builder` the block is handed. `indent` is a # count of spaces or the string one level is indented by. A block that # writes no value, or leaves a container open, is refused. def self.build(indent : String | Int32 | Nil = nil, & : (Builder -> Nil)) : String # The document read into `type`: `Nil`, `Bool`, `Int32`, `Int64`, `UInt8`, # `UInt64`, `Float64`, `String`, `Any`, a type with `derive serializable`, # one of those or `nil`, or an `Array` or `Hash(String, V)` of those. An # integer outside the type is refused, as is anything after the root # value. def self.from_json(str : String, type : T.class) : T forall T def initialize # The document as an `Any`; panics with the line and column of the first # thing it refuses. def self.parse(input : String) : Any # The document as an `Any`, or `nil` when it is not one. def self.parse?(input : String) : Any | ::Nil def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : Array(T).class) : Array(T) forall T def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : Hash(String, V).class) : Hash(String, V) forall V def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : Nil.class) : Nil def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : Bool.class) : Bool def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : Int32.class) : Int32 def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : Int64.class) : Int64 def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : UInt8.class) : UInt8 # An integer past Int64 reaches the reader as a float that still carries # its digits; those are read here, so the whole UInt64 range comes back. def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : UInt64.class) : UInt64 def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : Float64.class) : Float64 def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : String.class) : String def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : Any.class) : Any # A type that reads itself: the `initialize(pull)` a `derive # serializable` wrote. A type that admits nil reads `null` as the nil and # anything else as the other type (`x || raise`, as the derive asks it), # the way `write_or_null` writes it. That was `T.new(pull)` too, and # `Int32 | Nil` has no such `new`, so `JSON.from_json("5", Int32?)` and # `Array(Int32?)` did not build. def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : T.class) : T forall T # Any value `write_value` knows: `nil`, a `Bool`, a prelude integer, a # `Float64`, a `String`, an `Any`, an `Array` or `Hash` of those, or a type # that implements `ToJSON`; each of them or `nil`. def self.to_json(obj : T) : String forall T def self.write_value(val : Array(T), b : Builder) : Nil forall T # A String key is written as it is, and two of them are never one text. def self.write_value(val : Hash(String, V), b : Builder) : Nil forall V # Any other key is written by its `to_s`, `nil` as `"null"`, the word a # JSON null is, so two keys can be one text: `{nil => 1, "null" => 2}` # was written `{"null":1,"null":2}`, which `JSON.parse` refuses # ("duplicate key 'null' at line 1, column 11"). The texts written are # kept, and a repeat is refused, naming both keys. def self.write_value(val : Hash(K, V), b : Builder) : Nil forall K, V def self.write_value(val : Nil, b : Builder) : Nil def self.write_value(val : Bool, b : Builder) : Nil def self.write_value(val : Int32, b : Builder) : Nil def self.write_value(val : Int64, b : Builder) : Nil def self.write_value(val : UInt8, b : Builder) : Nil def self.write_value(val : UInt64, b : Builder) : Nil def self.write_value(val : Float64, b : Builder) : Nil def self.write_value(val : String, b : Builder) : Nil def self.write_value(val : Any, b : Builder) : Nil def self.write_value(val : T, b : Builder) : Nil forall T : ToJSON end # Reads a whole document into an `Any`. Like the lexer it records the first # failure instead of panicking; `JSON.parse` and `JSON.parse?` decide what to # do with it. pub class Parser def error : String | ::Nil def initialize(input : String) def parse : Any end # Reads a document one event at a time: `kind` names what the reader is on, # the `read_x` methods take it and move on. The grammar is checked as it is # read, so a missing comma or colon is refused where it is, with a panic. pub class PullParser enum Kind : Int32 Null = 0 Bool = 1 Int = 2 Float = 3 String = 4 BeginArray = 5 EndArray = 6 BeginObject = 7 EndObject = 8 EOF = 9 # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `BeginArray` def begin_array? : ::Bool # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `BeginObject` def begin_object? : ::Bool # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `Bool` def bool? : ::Bool # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `EndArray` def end_array? : ::Bool # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `EndObject` def end_object? : ::Bool # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `EOF` def eof? : ::Bool # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `Float` def float? : ::Bool # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `Int` def int? : ::Bool # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `Null` def null? : ::Bool # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `String` def string? : ::Bool end def bool_value : Bool def column_number : Int32 def float_value : Float64 def initialize(input : String) def int_value : Int64 def kind : Kind def line_number : Int32 def max_nesting : Int32 def max_nesting=(value : Int32) : Int32 # Reads an object, yields once at the value of `key`, and skips the rest. def on_key(key : String, & : (-> Nil)) : Nil # The number the reader is on, as it was written. def raw_value : String # The value the reader is on, as an `Any`. def read_any : Any def read_array(& : (-> Nil)) : Nil def read_begin_array : Nil def read_begin_object : Nil def read_bool : Bool def read_end_array : Nil def read_end_object : Nil # A float, or an integer read as one. def read_float : Float64 def read_int : Int64 def read_next : Kind def read_null : Nil def read_null? : Bool # Yields each key of the object the reader is on, with the reader at its # value. A key named twice is refused, as `JSON.parse` refuses it. def read_object(& : (String -> Nil)) : Nil def read_object_key : String # The value the reader is on, written into `json` as it is read. A number # is written as its own text, the text it was read from: rebuilt from the # Int64 or Float64 it parsed to, `12345678901234567890` came back as # `1.2345678901234567e+19` and `1E+2` as `100.0`, and a UInt64 id passed # through here did not read back as itself. def read_raw(json : Builder) : Nil # The value the reader is on, as JSON text. def read_raw : String def read_string : String # Passes over the value the reader is on, whole. def skip : Nil def string_value : String end # A type that can write itself into a `Builder`. `JSON.to_json` accepts any # value whose type implements it, as a `derive serializable` type does. pub trait ToJSON abstract def to_json(json : Builder) : Nil end impl ToJSON for Any def to_json(json : Builder) : Nil end
files.iyi doc std/kernel: module std/kernel # Terminates the program with *status*, after writing *message* to # standard error as a line, as `puts` writes one: a message that already # ends in a newline gets no second one, as in the other library. # # The ending is `exit`'s, as the other library's `abort` is its `exit`: # what the task deferred runs, and what a stream set to `sync = false` # holds is written. This wrote through the runtime's own `__iyi_write` and # ended with `__iyi_exit`, which skip both: `STDOUT.sync = false`, # `puts "before"`, `abort "bye"` left standard output empty, a `defer` # around the call never ran, and a line buffered on standard error before # the message was lost. pub def abort(message : String | ::Nil = nil, status : Int32 = 1) : NoReturn # Repeatedly executes the block until break. pub def loop(& : (-> Nil)) : Nil # Inspects object to standard output followed by newline. Returns object. pub def p(object : T) : T forall T # Inspects each object to standard output. Returns objects tuple. pub def p(*objects : *T) : Tuple(*T) forall T # Pretty prints object to standard output. Returns object. pub def pp(object : T) : T forall T # Pretty prints each object to standard output. Returns objects tuple. pub def pp(*objects : *T) : Tuple(*T) forall T # Prints objects without trailing newline. pub def print_all(*objects : *T) : Nil forall T # Prints objects followed by a newline. pub def puts_all(*objects : *T) : Nil forall T

files.iyi doc std/list: module std/list # The store is built at construction and never handed out, so no method of this # type can be observed to change it. That is what makes the value shareable # under III.4.4 — every field immutable after construction — and it is why the # constructor **copies**. # # The copy is not defensive habit, it is the missing borrow checker. `List` # cannot express "I own this array now", so a caller that kept a reference to # what it passed in could mutate the list from underneath a task holding it. # Rust says this with ownership and pays nothing; here it costs one copy at the # boundary, once, and it is the honest price of not having that machinery. pub struct List(T) # Two lists are the same value when they hold the same elements in the same # order, which is the whole of what a list is. Until this method, the one # answering was `Object#==` (src/iyi/object.iyi:37-39), the constant # `false` — not even reflexive, so `list == list` was false too, and every # collection that asks said no: `includes?`, `index` and `uniq` all go # through `==`, a list could never be found in a `Hash`, and a `case` over # a list matched no `when`, because a `when` is `===` and `===` is `==`. # That is the failure object.iyi:111-120 wrote up for `Tuple`, reproduced # by the one type III.4.7 added for handing a value between tasks — where # comparing what two tasks produced is the point. # # Sizes first, because that is the cheap half of the answer. No shared-store # fast path like `Slice#same?`: the constructor copies, so two lists never # share a store, and the comparison would pay for every call to fire only # when a list is compared with itself. # # Restricted to `List(T)`, so a list of another element type is unequal by # the prelude's default rather than a compile error — the reasoning # object.iyi:119-120 gives for restricting `Tuple#==` to its own shape. def ==(other : List(T)) : Bool # Indexed with `[]`, because every other sequence here is — `Slice` # (std/slice.iyi:107), the prelude's `Array` (src/iyi/array.iyi:78) and # everything under `Indexable` (std/indexable.iyi:75) — and III.1.7a says a # name shared with Crystal means the same thing here. A negative index # counts from the end, so `list[-1]` is the last element; that rule was # already true through the backing array and unwritten, which is worse than # either answer. # # The out-of-range sentence is raised here rather than left to the store. # The array's wording is the right wording — it names the index asked for # and how many elements there are, and names no receiver, so there is # nothing in it about an array the caller never handed over — but a message # this type promises is this file's, not one inherited by accident from a # field nobody can see. def [](index : Int32) : T # The nilable partner, which is the one question `[]` cannot answer: "the # element there, or nothing". Without it every caller probing a list past # its end rewrites the bounds rule above by hand against `size`, and two # copies of a rule is one too many. def []?(index : Int32) : T | ::Nil protected def adopt(items : Array(T)) : Nil # Every operation that would change a sequence returns a new one instead, so # by III.1.7's convention they are all participles. The plain verbs — `push`, # `sort`, `reverse` — name the mutating form, and this type has none. That the # naming rule falls out rather than being applied is the point of having # settled it before any library code existed. # # Each builds its array at the size it ends with, once. `dup` then `<<` # copied the list, grew the copy to twice its size and handed it to the # constructor, which copied it a third time: an append to a list of n # elements wrote 4n words where n + 1 is the whole of the work. def appended(item : T) : List(T) # `at` is the name this file had before `[]`, and samples/iyi/immutable.iyi # is written in it. It stays, spelled out, and delegates — so both names # exist but only one bounds rule does. def at(index : Int32) : T def concatenated(other : List(T)) : List(T) def empty? : Bool # Hashing follows equality, or the agreement above buys nothing: a `Hash` # finds a key by its slot first and compares second, so two equal lists in # different slots are still two keys. `Object#hash` answered with the type # id — every `List(Int32)` in one slot, "correct and useless" in exactly # the way object.iyi:20-23 says of a key type that never said how it # hashes. # # The array's own hash, which is `Indexable#hash`'s mixing (the prelude's # `Array#hash`): one function, so a list and the array it was built from # land in the same slot. def hash : Int32 def initialize(items : Array(T)) # Written down the same way it prints, because a list has no second form: # the elements inside it are already inspected. Stated rather than left to # `Object#inspect` so it is in this module's exported surface, which is # what a list nested in another collection is asked for — `List[List[1]]` # rather than a type name — and it is how `Slice` states it too. def inspect : String # A list over an array nothing else holds: the one `appended` or # `concatenated` has just built. The copy above is for a caller's array, # which the caller still has; one made here has no other owner. protected def self.owning(items : Array(T)) : List(T) def size : Int32 # A list prints its elements, like both of its siblings: `Slice[10, 20, 30]` # and the array's `[10, 20, 30]`. Inherited, it printed # `Std::List::List(Int32)`, which object.iyi:7-8 calls what "a value that # has said nothing about itself can honestly print" — and a sequence has # plenty to say, so the default was the type failing to answer. # # The elements are *inspected* rather than printed, which is `Slice#to_s`'s # reasoning (std/slice.iyi:353-364): a list of strings reads back as # `List["pear", "fig"]`, telling a reader the elements are strings, where # printing them loses that with no way to get it back. def to_s : String end # And the lazy half, for the same reason `std/slice` has one: a `List` could # only reach the iterator tower through `to_a`, which copies the sequence # the type exists to hand around without copying. # # A class, as `ArrayIterator` is (std/iterator.iyi): an adaptor keeps its # source by value, and this struct was copied into it, so # `it.first(2).to_a` and then `it.to_a` gave [1, 2] and [1, 2, 3, 4] where # an iterator over an array gives [1, 2] and [3, 4]. pub class ListIterator(T) def initialize(list : List(T)) def next : T | Stop end impl Std::Enumerable::Enumerable for List(T) forall T def each(& : (T -> Nil)) : Nil end impl Std::Iterator::Iterator for ListIterator(T) forall T end

: Bool end pub class MemoryBackend < Backend def clear : Nil def close : Nil def entries : Array(Entry) def formatter : Formatter def formatter=(value : Formatter) : Formatter def initialize(formatter : Formatter = DefaultFormatter.new) # The entries as the formatter would have written them. def output : Array(String) def write(entry : Entry) : Nil end pub enum Severity : Int32 Trace = 0 Debug = 1 Info = 2 Notice = 3 Warn = 4 Error = 5 Fatal = 6 None = 7 def <(other : Severity) : Bool def <=(other : Severity) : Bool def >(other : Severity) : Bool def >=(other : Severity) : Bool def label : String def self.parse(name : String) : Severity # The severity named by *name*, case-insensitively, or nil: what a # `LOG_LEVEL` variable holds. def self.parse?(name : String) : Severity | ::Nil def to_s : String end
